summary: Built by Atlantic City in 1917 near McKee City and reported as South Jersey's first permanent fire lookout; the register says it reached 100 feet after a 1946 addition.

facts.design: Aermotor tower with a 7x7-foot metal cab, raised to 100 feet by a 20-foot addition in 1946 (per NHLR)

events.note: State Fire Warden selected a site on the Mays Landing road near McKee City; the city was to pay for the tower
Atlantic City watch tower near its watershed; 1917 newspapers give 60 to 65 feet; the register calls it wooden and iron-braced, built by the coast resort water department
State report calls it the first permanent Forest Fire Lookout in South Jersey
Manned throughout the 1917-18 season, per a later state annual report
Register says the state built an 80-foot Aermotor tower; no second source found
A 20-foot addition raised the tower to 100 feet, per the register

evidence.supports: first a wooden, iron-braced tower built in 1917 by the coast resort water department; just west of Atlantic City
evidence.quote: Located just west of Atlantic City, NJ, McKeetown Fire Tower was first a wooden and iron braced tower built by the coast resort water department in 1917.

evidence.supports: state built 80-foot Aermotor in 1924; 20-foot addition in 1946 raised it to 100 feet
evidence.quote: The state built this 80’ Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab in 1924. In 1946 a 20’ addition was clamped to the top, raising the tower to its current 100’.
Administered by New Jersey Forest Fire Service

evidence.supports: 1916 site selected on the Mays Landing road near McKee City by the State Fire Warden
evidence.quote: a site for the erection of a high lookout tower on Mays Landing road near McKee City was selected yesterday by State Fire Warden Charles P. Wilber

evidence.supports: city to pay for the tower; aim to conserve county forests and the city water supply
evidence.quote: The city is to defray the expense of erecting the tower
A fire tower, sixty feet high, from which can be observed the location of any forest fires in Atlantic County woodland, is being erected on the Pleasantville-Mays Landing road.

evidence.supports: enclosed room at the top for a state-supplied watchman
evidence.quote: On the top of the frame work will be an enclosed room for the use of the watchmen, who will be supplied by the State
The tower is sixty-five feet high.

evidence.supports: 1917 state report: first permanent forest fire lookout in South Jersey
evidence.quote: Atlantic City has made possible the institution at McKeetown, Atlantic County, of the first permanent Forest Fire Lookout in South Jersey.
has been manned throughout the season

evidence.quote: McKeetown Station 75 feet (23 m) 100 feet (30 m) Div. C Sec. C6, C7,(C4, C5) Egg Harbor Township

evidence.supports: listed among towers in active service
1916 article dated June 17, 1916 (site selected the day before)
1916 aim: conserve county forests and, through them, the city water supply
evidence.quote: As an aid to conserving the county forests, and through this means the city's water supply

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register puts the tower just west of Atlantic City, while Wikipedia's table lists Egg Harbor Township. Both are in Atlantic County; the story gives the register's wording and notes the Wikipedia listing.

notes_for_editor: The 1916-1919 history comes from 1916-1919 newspaper and state report clippings reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page. The 1924 state tower and the 1946 addition come from the NHLR page only. The 1917 newspapers give 60 to 65 feet, and the register's 80 feet belongs to the 1924 tower; no source confirms whether the 1924 tower replaced or enlarged the 1917 one, so this stays open. No current staffing or public-access source was found, and the Wikipedia active-service heading is undated, so the staffing and access facts are omitted. The NHLR page has no photo reused here; the existing Wikimedia Commons photo in the record is kept.
